title: Key English Idioms with Gujarati & English Meanings and Examples
description: A curated collection of common English idioms. Each entry includes the idiom, its English meaning, its Gujarati meaning (ગુજરાતી અર્થ), and 3-5 example sentences showing real usage.

idioms.english_meaning: Something that seems bad or unlucky at first but results in something good later.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: છૂપો આશીર્વાદ; શરૂઆતમાં ખરાબ લાગતી પણ પાછળથી સારી સાબિત થતી ઘટના.
examples: Losing that job turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
It pushed me to start my own business.
Within a year I was earning twice as much.
Sometimes a setback is really a blessing in disguise.

idioms.english_meaning: To endure a painful or unpleasant situation that is unavoidable.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મુશ્કેલ કે અપ્રિય પરિસ્થિતિને હિંમતથી સ્વીકારી લેવી; દાંત ભીંસીને સહન કરવું.
examples: The dentist appointment was scary, but I decided to bite the bullet.
I had been avoiding it for months.
Finally I booked the slot and went in.
It hurt a little, but I felt relieved afterward.

idioms.english_meaning: To do or say something to relieve tension and start a conversation in an awkward situation.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ઔપચારિકતા કે અસહજતા તોડીને વાતચીત શરૂ કરવી; પ્રથમ સંકોચ દૂર કરવો.
examples: The party was silent when the guests arrived.
To break the ice, the host started a fun game.
Soon everyone was laughing and chatting.
A small joke can easily break the ice.
Asking about someone's hobbies is a great way to break the ice.

idioms.idiom: The ball is in your court
idioms.english_meaning: It is your turn to make a decision or take the next action.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: હવે નિર્ણય કે પગલું તમારે લેવાનું છે; દડો હવે તમારી બાજુ છે.
examples: I have made my offer to you.
I explained all the terms clearly.
Now the ball is in your court.
Let me know your decision by tomorrow.

idioms.idiom: Hit the nail on the head
idioms.english_meaning: To describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem; to be precisely right.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: બરાબર સાચી વાત કહેવી; નિશાન પર ચોટ મારવી.
examples: Everyone was confused about why sales dropped.
Then Riya said it was a pricing problem.
She hit the nail on the head.
Once we fixed the price, sales recovered.

idioms.english_meaning: Something that happens very rarely.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ખૂબ ભાગ્યે જ; ક્યારેક ક્યારેક જ બનતી દુર્લભ ઘટના.
examples: My brother lives in another country.
He visits us only once in a blue moon.
So when he comes, we celebrate a lot.
Such rare visits feel very special.

idioms.english_meaning: Something that is very easy to do.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ખૂબ સહેલું કામ; રમત-વાત જેવું સરળ.
examples: I was nervous about the math test.
But the questions were very simple.
The whole exam was a piece of cake.
I finished it in half the time.

idioms.idiom: Let the cat out of the bag
idioms.english_meaning: To reveal a secret carelessly or by mistake.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: અજાણતાં કે ભૂલથી રહસ્ય ખુલ્લું પાડી દેવું; ગુપ્ત વાત જાહેર કરી દેવી.
examples: We were planning a surprise party for Mom.
But my little sister let the cat out of the bag.
She told Mom about the cake.
The surprise was ruined.

idioms.idiom: Cost an arm and a leg
idioms.english_meaning: To be very expensive.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ખૂબ મોંઘું હોવું; ભારે કિંમત ચૂકવવી પડે એવું.
examples: I really wanted that new phone.
But it cost an arm and a leg.
I decided to wait for a discount.
Saving money is better than overspending.

idioms.english_meaning: Feeling slightly ill or unwell.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: તબિયત થોડી નરમ હોવી; બીમાર જેવું લાગવું.
examples: I did not go to office today.
I was feeling under the weather.
My head was aching and I felt tired.
After some rest, I felt much better.

idioms.english_meaning: To reveal secret information, often unintentionally.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: રહસ્ય ઉઘાડું પાડી દેવું; છૂપી વાત કહી દેવી.
examples: Everyone wanted to know the trip plan.
Finally Arjun spilled the beans.
He told us we were going to Goa.
We all got excited immediately.

idioms.english_meaning: To work or study late into the night.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મોડી રાત સુધી મહેનત કરવી કે ભણવું; રાત-દિવસ એક કરવો.
examples: The exams were just a week away.
I had a lot of syllabus to cover.
So I burned the midnight oil every day.
My hard work paid off with good marks.

idioms.english_meaning: To do something cheaply or quickly by skipping proper steps, often reducing quality.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ગુણવત્તાનો ભોગ આપીને ઝડપથી કે સસ્તામાં કામ પતાવવું; શોર્ટકટ મારવો.
examples: The builder wanted to finish quickly.
So he cut corners on the construction.
Within months, the walls developed cracks.
Cutting corners often costs more later.

idioms.english_meaning: To become difficult or impossible to control.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કાબૂ બહાર જવું; પરિસ્થિતિ બેકાબૂ બની જવી.
examples: The argument started over a small matter.
But soon it got out of hand.
People began shouting at each other.
A teacher had to step in to calm everyone.

idioms.english_meaning: To go to bed; to go to sleep.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સૂવા જવું; પથારીમાં પડવું.
examples: It was already past midnight.
I was extremely tired after the long day.
So I decided to hit the sack.
I fell asleep the moment I lay down.

idioms.english_meaning: To joke with someone by telling them something untrue in a playful way.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મજાક-મસ્તીમાં કોઈને બનાવવું; ગમ્મત કરવી.
examples: My friend said I had won a lottery.
I got very excited for a moment.
Then I realised he was just pulling my leg.
We both laughed about it later.

idioms.english_meaning: A situation where you can enjoy the advantages of two different things at the same time.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: બે ફાયદાઓ એકસાથે મળવા; બંને બાજુનો લાભ.
examples: She works from home three days a week.
She goes to the office on the other days.
So she gets the best of both worlds.
She enjoys both comfort and teamwork.

idioms.english_meaning: Said when a person appears just after you were talking about them.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જેની વાત ચાલતી હોય તે જ વ્યક્તિ આવી ચડે ત્યારે વપરાતું વાક્ય.
examples: We were just talking about Rohan.
Suddenly he walked through the door.
Speak of the devil, we all said.
Everyone burst out laughing.

idioms.english_meaning: To make a bad situation worse by your words or actions.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: આગમાં ઘી હોમવું; ખરાબ પરિસ્થિતિને વધુ બગાડવી.
examples: The two friends were already arguing.
Then someone made a rude comment.
That just added fuel to the fire.
Their fight became much worse.

idioms.english_meaning: To avoid talking about the main point; to speak indirectly.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મુદ્દાની વાત ટાળીને આડી-અવળી વાત કરવી; આડ-વાટે વાત કરવી.
examples: I asked him directly about the money.
But he kept beating around the bush.
He talked about everything except the loan.
Finally I asked him to be straightforward.

idioms.english_meaning: To stop working on something for the rest of the day.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: દિવસનું કામ બંધ કરવું; આજ માટે કામ સમેટવું.
examples: We had been painting since morning.
By evening we were completely exhausted.
So we decided to call it a day.
We planned to finish the rest tomorrow.

idioms.english_meaning: To waste time worrying about something that has already happened and cannot be changed.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ભૂતકાળની ભૂલ માટે નકામો અફસોસ કરવો; ઢોળાયેલા દૂધ પર રડવું.
examples: I broke my favourite watch by mistake.
I felt sad about it for days.
Then I realised there was no use crying over spilt milk.
I simply bought a new one.

idioms.idiom: Every cloud has a silver lining
idioms.english_meaning: Every difficult situation has some positive aspect or hope.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: દરેક મુશ્કેલીમાં કોઈક આશા છૂપાયેલી હોય છે; દુઃખ પછી સુખ.
examples: He failed in his first business attempt.
But he learned many valuable lessons.
Every cloud has a silver lining.
His next venture became a big success.

idioms.english_meaning: To suddenly become nervous or hesitant about doing something planned.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: છેલ્લી ઘડીએ ગભરાઈ જવું કે હિંમત હારી જવી.
examples: She was ready to give the speech.
But just before going on stage, she got cold feet.
Her hands started shaking.
With some encouragement, she finally spoke well.

idioms.idiom: Kill two birds with one stone
idioms.english_meaning: To achieve two goals with a single action.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: એક પંથ દો કાજ; એક જ ક્રિયાથી બે કામ પૂરા કરવા.
examples: I went to the market for groceries.
On the way, I also paid the electricity bill.
I killed two birds with one stone.
It saved me an extra trip.

idioms.english_meaning: Something that happens suddenly and unexpectedly.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: અચાનક અને અણધાર્યું; એકાએક બની જતું.
examples: I had not seen my old friend for years.
One day, out of the blue, he called me.
I was completely surprised to hear his voice.
We talked for hours like old times.

idioms.english_meaning: To have the same understanding or agreement about something.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: એક જ વિચાર કે સમજ પર હોવું; સહમત હોવું.
examples: Before starting the project, we had a meeting.
We discussed every detail carefully.
We wanted to be on the same page.
This avoided confusion later.

idioms.english_meaning: To give up or admit defeat.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: હાર સ્વીકારી લેવી; પ્રયત્ન છોડી દેવો.
examples: The team was losing badly.
Many players wanted to throw in the towel.
But the captain refused to give up.
Their persistence almost turned the game around.

idioms.english_meaning: To tell someone angrily what you think about their bad behaviour (to give someone a piece of your mind).
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈને ગુસ્સામાં ખરી-ખોટી સંભળાવવી; મનની વાત ઠપકા સાથે કહેવી.
examples: The shopkeeper sold me a faulty product.
I went back and gave him a piece of my mind.
I told him never to cheat customers.
He apologised and refunded my money.

idioms.english_meaning: To start again from the beginning because the previous attempt failed.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ફરી શરૂઆતથી શરૂ કરવું; નવેસરથી યોજના બનાવવી.
examples: Our first design was rejected by the client.
We had to go back to the drawing board.
We brainstormed completely new ideas.
The second design was finally approved.

idioms.english_meaning: To try very hard, often more than expected, to help or please someone.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈને મદદ કરવા માટે ખૂબ જ મહેનત કરવી; પૂરો પ્રયત્ન કરવો.
examples: The hotel staff were very kind.
They bent over backwards to make us comfortable.
They arranged everything we asked for.
We had a wonderful stay there.

idioms.english_meaning: To destroy relationships or connections, making it impossible to go back.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સંબંધો કાયમ માટે તોડી નાખવા; પાછા ફરવાનો રસ્તો બંધ કરી દેવો.
examples: He left his job in anger.
He insulted his manager on the way out.
He burned his bridges with the company.
Later he regretted not staying polite.

idioms.idiom: Cross that bridge when you come to it
idioms.english_meaning: To deal with a problem only when it actually happens, not before.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જે સમસ્યા આવે ત્યારે જ તેનો સામનો કરવો; અગાઉથી ચિંતા ન કરવી.
examples: I was worried about the final round of interviews.
My friend told me not to stress yet.
We will cross that bridge when we come to it.
First, I should focus on the next round.

idioms.english_meaning: To get to the main point without wasting time.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: આડ-વાત છોડીને સીધી મુદ્દાની વાત પર આવવું.
examples: The meeting was running too long.
The manager asked everyone to cut to the chase.
We quickly discussed the main decisions.
The meeting ended on time after that.

idioms.english_meaning: Practical, humble, and realistic; not proud.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જમીન સાથે જોડાયેલું; નમ્ર અને વ્યવહારુ સ્વભાવ.
examples: Despite being very rich, he is very simple.
He talks to everyone politely.
He is a down to earth person.
Everyone respects him for his humility.

idioms.english_meaning: To accept and deal with the unpleasant consequences of one's actions.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પોતાના કાર્યના પરિણામોનો સામનો કરવો; ભૂલની સજા સ્વીકારવી.
examples: He had broken the school rules.
Now he had to face the music.
The principal called him to the office.
He accepted his punishment quietly.

idioms.english_meaning: To learn how to do something after some practice.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પ્રેક્ટિસથી કોઈ કામ શીખી જવું; ફાવટ આવી જવી.
examples: Driving felt difficult on the first day.
I kept making small mistakes.
But after a week, I got the hang of it.
Now I can drive confidently.

idioms.idiom: Give the benefit of the doubt
idioms.english_meaning: To believe something good about someone rather than something bad, when you are not sure.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: શંકા હોવા છતાં કોઈ પર ભરોસો રાખવો; સારી રીતે માની લેવું.
examples: He was late again for the meeting.
But he said his train was delayed.
I gave him the benefit of the doubt.
I chose to trust his explanation.

idioms.english_meaning: To make more effort than is expected or required.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: અપેક્ષા કરતાં વધારે મહેનત કરવી; એક ડગલું આગળ વધવું.
examples: She always goes the extra mile at work.
She stays late to help her teammates.
Her dedication is admired by everyone.
That is why she got promoted quickly.

idioms.english_meaning: To be in the same difficult situation as someone else.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: એક જ મુશ્કેલ પરિસ્થિતિમાં હોવું; એક જ નાવમાં સવાર હોવું.
examples: Many students failed the difficult test.
I was not the only one who struggled.
We were all in the same boat.
So we decided to study together next time.

idioms.english_meaning: To watch someone or something carefully.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ધ્યાન રાખવું; નજર રાખવી.
examples: I had to step out for a few minutes.
I asked my neighbour to keep an eye on my house.
She watched it carefully while I was away.
Everything was safe when I returned.

idioms.english_meaning: To avoid bringing up an old problem or conflict that could cause trouble.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જૂની વાત કે ઝઘડો ઉખેળવો નહિ; શાંત મામલાને છંછેડવો નહિ.
examples: The two cousins had fought years ago.
Now they were finally friendly again.
We decided to let sleeping dogs lie.
No one mentioned the old argument.

idioms.english_meaning: To earn just enough money to cover one's basic needs.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મુશ્કેલીથી ઘરખર્ચ ચલાવવો; બે છેડા ભેગા કરવા.
examples: After he lost his job, life became hard.
He took up two part-time jobs.
He worked hard just to make ends meet.
Slowly his situation began to improve.

idioms.english_meaning: To miss an opportunity because of being too slow to act.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મોડું થવાથી તક ગુમાવી દેવી; મોકો ચૂકી જવો.
examples: The offer had a huge discount.
I kept thinking about it for too long.
By the time I decided, I had missed the boat.
The sale was already over.

idioms.english_meaning: You cannot achieve success without effort and hard work.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મહેનત વિના ફળ નથી; દુઃખ વેઠ્યા વિના સફળતા નથી.
examples: Training for the marathon was very tough.
My muscles ached every single day.
But no pain, no gain, I reminded myself.
Finally I completed the race proudly.

idioms.english_meaning: In a risky or dangerous situation where one mistake could cause trouble.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જોખમભરી પરિસ્થિતિમાં હોવું; પાતળા બરફ પર ચાલવા જેવું.
examples: He had already been warned twice at work.
Now he was on thin ice with his boss.
One more mistake could cost him his job.
So he started working very carefully.

idioms.english_meaning: To regain control of your emotions and become calm.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પોતાની જાતને સંભાળી લેવી; શાંત થઈ જવું.
examples: She was crying after the bad news.
Her friend asked her to pull herself together.
She took a deep breath and calmed down.
Soon she was ready to face the situation.

idioms.english_meaning: To spoil someone's happiness or plans.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈની ખુશી કે યોજનામાં ભંગ પાડવો; આનંદ બગાડવો.
examples: She was thrilled about her new idea.
I did not want to rain on her parade.
So I encouraged her instead of criticising.
She appreciated my support a lot.

idioms.english_meaning: To agree completely with someone.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પૂરી રીતે સહમત હોવું; એકમત હોવું.
examples: The two partners run a business together.
They do not always see eye to eye.
But they respect each other's opinions.
Their differences make the business stronger.

idioms.english_meaning: To avoid making a decision or choosing a side.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: નિર્ણય ન લેવો; બંને બાજુ રહીને કોઈ પક્ષ ન લેવો.
examples: Everyone shared their opinion in the debate.
But he kept sitting on the fence.
He refused to support either side.
Finally we asked him to make a choice.

idioms.english_meaning: To take attention or credit away from someone else.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈની વાહવાહી કે શ્રેય છીનવી લેવો; કોઈનું ધ્યાન ખેંચી લેવું.
examples: She had prepared the whole presentation.
But her colleague announced the results first.
He stole her thunder in front of the boss.
She felt upset about not getting credit.

idioms.idiom: Take it with a grain of salt
idioms.english_meaning: To not completely believe something; to be doubtful about it.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ વાત પૂરી રીતે માની ન લેવી; શંકા સાથે સ્વીકારવી.
examples: He often exaggerates his stories.
So I take whatever he says with a grain of salt.
I never believe him completely.
It is wiser to check the facts myself.

idioms.english_meaning: A small, visible part of a much larger problem.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મોટી સમસ્યાનો માત્ર નાનો દેખાતો ભાગ; હિમશિલાનો છેડો.
examples: The company found a few errors in the report.
But that was just the tip of the iceberg.
A deeper check revealed many more mistakes.
They had to redo the entire audit.

idioms.english_meaning: To stay loyal and supportive in both good and bad times.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સુખ-દુઃખ બંનેમાં સાથ આપવો; દરેક પરિસ્થિતિમાં વફાદાર રહેવું.
examples: My best friend has always supported me.
She stood by me through thick and thin.
She helped me during my toughest days.
Such friends are very rare to find.

idioms.english_meaning: To deliberately ignore something wrong.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જાણીજોઈને કોઈ ખોટી વાત તરફ આંખ આડા કાન કરવા; અવગણના કરવી.
examples: The guard saw the boys breaking the rule.
But he turned a blind eye to it.
He did not want any trouble.
Later the manager scolded him for ignoring it.

idioms.english_meaning: Uncertain or not yet decided.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: અનિશ્ચિત; હજુ નક્કી ન થયેલું.
examples: We wanted to go on a holiday this month.
But our plans are still up in the air.
We have not booked anything yet.
We will decide once everyone is free.

idioms.english_meaning: Something that will never happen.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ક્યારેય ન બને એવી વાત; અશક્ય બાબત.
examples: He said he would clean his room daily.
His sister laughed and said, when pigs fly.
She knew he would never keep that promise.
Sure enough, the room stayed messy.

idioms.idiom: Bite off more than you can chew
idioms.english_meaning: To take on more work or responsibility than you can handle.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પોતાની શક્તિ કરતાં વધારે કામ માથે લેવું; ગજા બહારનું કામ સ્વીકારવું.
examples: He agreed to manage three projects at once.
Soon he realised he had bitten off more than he could chew.
He could not meet any of the deadlines.
He learned to take on less work next time.

idioms.english_meaning: What you do matters more than what you say.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: વાતો કરતાં કાર્ય વધુ મહત્ત્વનું હોય છે; બોલવા કરતાં કરી બતાવવું.
examples: He kept promising to help the poor.
But he never actually did anything.
Actions speak louder than words.
People believe deeds, not just speeches.

idioms.idiom: The early bird catches the worm
idioms.english_meaning: The person who acts first or arrives early gets the best opportunity.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: વહેલા ઊઠનાર કે પહેલ કરનારને શ્રેષ્ઠ તક મળે છે; વહેલો તે પહેલો.
examples: She reached the sale an hour before opening.
The early bird catches the worm.
She grabbed the best items at low prices.
Others arrived late and found empty shelves.

idioms.english_meaning: Very common and easy to find; not special or valuable.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: બહુ સામાન્ય અને સહેલાઈથી મળી રહે એવું; કોઈ ખાસ મૂલ્ય વગરનું.
examples: Cheap plastic toys are a dime a dozen these days.
You can find them in every street shop.
That is why they cost almost nothing.
Good quality toys, however, are hard to find.

idioms.english_meaning: To pursue a mistaken or misguided course of action.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ખોટી દિશામાં પ્રયત્ન કરવો; ખોટા માણસ કે કારણ પાછળ પડવું.
examples: The police suspected the neighbour at first.
But they were barking up the wrong tree.
The real thief was someone else entirely.
They had to restart the whole investigation.

idioms.english_meaning: To reach the required standard; to succeed or be good enough.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જરૂરી ધોરણ સુધી પહોંચવું; અપેક્ષા પ્રમાણે સફળ થવું.
examples: The new player trained very hard.
Everyone wondered if he could cut the mustard.
In the final match, he scored the winning goal.
He proved that he was good enough.

idioms.english_meaning: To leave a place or begin a journey.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: નીકળી પડવું; પ્રવાસ શરૂ કરવો.
examples: We packed our bags early in the morning.
It was time to hit the road.
We had a long drive ahead of us.
We reached the hills by evening.

idioms.english_meaning: To join an activity or trend because it has become popular.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: લોકપ્રિય બની ગયેલા વલણ કે પ્રવૃત્તિમાં જોડાઈ જવું; ભીડ પાછળ ચાલવું.
examples: When the new app became famous, everyone downloaded it.
Many people jumped on the bandwagon overnight.
They used it only because others did.
A few months later, most of them stopped.

idioms.english_meaning: To release stress, anger, or strong emotion in a harmless way.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મનનો ઉભરો કે ગુસ્સો કાઢી નાખવો; તણાવ હળવો કરવો.
examples: After a stressful week, he went for a long run.
Exercising helped him let off steam.
He came back feeling calm and fresh.
Everyone needs a healthy way to relax.

idioms.idiom: Off the top of my head
idioms.english_meaning: Saying something from memory, without checking or thinking carefully.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: વિચાર્યા કે તપાસ્યા વગર સ્મૃતિના આધારે તરત કહેવું.
examples: Someone asked me for the exact figures.
Off the top of my head, I said around fifty.
I told them I would confirm the real number later.
After checking, it was actually fifty-three.

idioms.english_meaning: To use one's influence or connections to get an advantage.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પોતાની ઓળખાણ કે વગનો ઉપયોગ કરીને કામ કઢાવવું.
examples: He got the appointment unusually quickly.
Clearly someone had pulled a few strings.
An ordinary person would have waited for weeks.
Connections often open doors faster.

idioms.english_meaning: The final small problem that makes a situation unbearable.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સહનશક્તિ તોડી નાખતી છેલ્લી નાની ઘટના; હદ વટાવી દેતી વાત.
examples: She had tolerated his rudeness for months.
His insult that day was the last straw.
She finally decided to quit the job.
Sometimes one small thing ends a lot of patience.

idioms.english_meaning: To take a big risk and stop worrying about the consequences.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પરિણામની ચિંતા છોડીને મોટું જોખમ ઉઠાવવું.
examples: He had always played it safe with money.
One day he threw caution to the wind.
He invested his savings in a new idea.
Luckily, the gamble paid off well.

idioms.english_meaning: To stop yourself from saying something you really want to say.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મોઢે આવેલી વાત રોકી લેવી; બોલતાં બોલતાં અટકી જવું.
examples: I strongly disagreed with my boss.
But I had to bite my tongue in the meeting.
Saying it openly could have caused trouble.
I shared my opinion politely afterwards.

idioms.idiom: By the skin of your teeth
idioms.english_meaning: To succeed or escape by a very narrow margin.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: માંડ માંડ; ખૂબ થોડા અંતરથી બચી જવું કે સફળ થવું.
examples: I reached the airport very late.
I caught my flight by the skin of my teeth.
Another minute and I would have missed it.
I promised myself never to be late again.

idioms.english_meaning: To be very expensive.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ઘણું મોંઘું પડવું; મોટી રકમ ખર્ચાવી.
examples: The wedding decorations looked stunning.
But they must have cost a pretty penny.
The family had saved for years for this day.
Everyone agreed it was worth the money.

idioms.idiom: Get a taste of your own medicine
idioms.english_meaning: To receive the same bad treatment that you gave to others.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જેવું વર્તન બીજા સાથે કર્યું હોય તેવું જ વર્તન પોતાને ભોગવવું પડે; જેવા સાથે તેવા.
examples: He always teased his classmates unkindly.
One day they all teased him back together.
He finally got a taste of his own medicine.
After that, he became more considerate.

idioms.english_meaning: To begin studying seriously.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મન લગાવીને ભણવા બેસવું; ચોપડીઓ ખોલવી.
examples: The final exams were getting closer.
It was time to hit the books.
I made a timetable and studied daily.
My efforts showed in the results.

idioms.english_meaning: In trouble or a difficult situation because of something you did.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મુશ્કેલીમાં મુકાવું; આફતમાં ફસાવું.
examples: He forgot to submit the important report.
Now he was in hot water with his manager.
He had to explain the delay seriously.
He stayed late to fix the mistake.

idioms.english_meaning: To stay cheerful and hopeful during a difficult time.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મુશ્કેલીમાં હિંમત રાખવી; હસતા રહેવું.
examples: She was upset after failing the interview.
Her friend told her to keep her chin up.
Better opportunities were surely waiting.
She smiled and started preparing again.

idioms.english_meaning: To wait for a situation to become calm before acting.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પરિસ્થિતિ શાંત થાય ત્યાં સુધી રાહ જોવી; ધૂળ બેસવા દેવી.
examples: There was a big argument in the office.
We decided to let the dust settle first.
After a few days, everyone was calmer.
Then we discussed the matter peacefully.

idioms.english_meaning: Extremely happy and joyful.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ખૂબ જ ખુશ; આનંદથી ઝૂમી ઊઠવું.
examples: She received the job offer of her dreams.
She was on cloud nine all day.
She called everyone to share the news.
Her happiness was clear on her face.

idioms.english_meaning: To pay much more than something is worth.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ વસ્તુ માટે ભારે કિંમત ચૂકવવી; ગજા બહારની કિંમત આપવી.
examples: The hotel during the festival was costly.
We had to pay through the nose for one night.
Prices doubled because of the crowd.
Next time we will book well in advance.

idioms.english_meaning: Everything that is possible or available; the full extent.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: બધું જ; પૂરેપૂરું, કંઈ બાકી રાખ્યા વગર.
examples: For her birthday, they planned everything.
Balloons, cake, music, gifts, the whole nine yards.
No detail was left out.
It turned out to be a grand celebration.

idioms.english_meaning: A way of asking what someone is quietly thinking about.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: તું શું વિચારે છે એમ પ્રેમથી પૂછવાની રીત.
examples: She sat by the window looking lost.
A penny for your thoughts, I asked gently.
She smiled and shared what was on her mind.
Sometimes people just need to talk.

idioms.idiom: Burn the candle at both ends
idioms.english_meaning: To exhaust yourself by being busy from early morning till late night.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: આરામ વગર સવારથી રાત સુધી મહેનત કરીને થાકી જવું.
examples: He worked all day and studied all night.
He was burning the candle at both ends.
Soon his health began to suffer.
He learned that rest is also important.

idioms.english_meaning: To raise a false alarm so often that people stop believing you.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: વારંવાર ખોટી ભડક ઊભી કરવી; એમ કે પછી સાચું કહો તોય કોઈ માને નહિ.
examples: The boy joked about danger many times.
He had cried wolf too often.
When real trouble came, no one believed him.
False alarms destroy your credibility.

idioms.english_meaning: To start an activity or process.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ કામ કે પ્રક્રિયાની શરૂઆત કરવી.
examples: The project had been delayed for too long.
We finally decided to get the ball rolling.
The first task was assigned to the team.
Once started, the work moved quickly.

idioms.english_meaning: To wait, slow down, or be more patient.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જરા થોભો; ઉતાવળ ન કરો.
examples: He wanted to buy the car immediately.
Hold your horses, his father said.
They first checked the engine carefully.
Patience saved them from a bad deal.

idioms.english_meaning: To act too soon, before the right time.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સમય પહેલાં ઉતાવળે પગલું લેવું.
examples: She announced the results before confirming them.
She had jumped the gun.
Later the figures turned out to be wrong.
It is better to wait for certainty.

idioms.english_meaning: To prevent something unpleasant from coming too close.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ ખરાબ વસ્તુને દૂર રાખવી; નજીક આવવા ન દેવી.
examples: A healthy diet helps keep illness at bay.
He ate well and exercised daily.
This kept many diseases at bay.
Prevention is always better than cure.

idioms.idiom: Like two peas in a pod
idioms.english_meaning: Two people who are very similar or always together.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: એકબીજાને ખૂબ મળતા આવતા કે હંમેશા સાથે રહેતા બે જણ.
examples: The twin sisters do everything together.
They are like two peas in a pod.
They even dress in the same style.
It is hard to tell them apart.

idioms.idiom: Out of the frying pan into the fire
idioms.english_meaning: To go from a bad situation to an even worse one.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: એક મુશ્કેલીમાંથી નીકળીને બીજી મોટી મુશ્કેલીમાં પડવું.
examples: He quit his stressful job in a hurry.
His new job was far more stressful.
He had jumped out of the frying pan into the fire.
He wished he had thought it through.

idioms.idiom: Put all your eggs in one basket
idioms.english_meaning: To risk everything on a single plan or option.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: બધું જોખમ એક જ જગ્યાએ લગાવી દેવું; બધા ઈંડા એક જ ટોપલીમાં મૂકવા.
examples: He invested all his money in one company.
He had put all his eggs in one basket.
When the company failed, he lost everything.
Spreading risk is always wiser.

idioms.english_meaning: To understand a hidden or unstated meaning.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: શબ્દોની પાછળનો છૂપો અર્થ સમજવો; બે લીટી વચ્ચેનું વાંચવું.
examples: Her message sounded polite on the surface.
But if you read between the lines, she was upset.
I understood that she needed support.
I called her right away to talk.

idioms.english_meaning: To sell very quickly and in large numbers.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ધડાધડ વેચાઈ જવું; ખૂબ ઝડપથી વેચાવું.
examples: The new phone was launched yesterday.
It is selling like hot cakes.
Most stores are already out of stock.
People are pre-booking the next batch.

idioms.idiom: Take the bull by the horns
idioms.english_meaning: To deal with a difficult situation bravely and directly.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મુશ્કેલીનો હિંમતપૂર્વક અને સીધો સામનો કરવો.
examples: The company was facing serious losses.
The new manager took the bull by the horns.
She made bold decisions to fix the problems.
Within a year, the company recovered.

idioms.idiom: The grass is always greener on the other side
idioms.english_meaning: Other people's situations always seem better than your own.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: બીજાની પરિસ્થિતિ હંમેશા સારી લાગે છે; પારકી થાળીમાં ઘી વધારે દેખાય.
examples: He always envied his friend's job.
But the grass is always greener on the other side.
His friend actually had many problems too.
He learned to value what he had.

idioms.english_meaning: Something right in front of you that you fail to notice.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: નજર સામે હોવા છતાં ધ્યાનમાં ન આવવું.
examples: I searched everywhere for my keys.
They were right under my nose on the table.
I had simply overlooked them.
We often miss what is closest to us.

idioms.idiom: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
idioms.english_meaning: It is better to keep what you have than to risk it for more.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: હાથમાંનું એક પંખી ઝાડ પરના બેથી સારું; જે છે તે જાળવવું વધુ સારું.
examples: He was offered a safe, steady salary.
Another company promised more but was uncertain.
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
He wisely kept the secure job.

idioms.english_meaning: To finish something before the time runs out.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સમય પૂરો થાય તે પહેલાં કામ પતાવી દેવું.
examples: We had only an hour to submit the form.
We rushed to beat the clock.
We uploaded it just in time.
It was a close but successful finish.

idioms.english_meaning: To end a quarrel and make peace.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ઝઘડો ભૂલીને સમાધાન કરી લેવું; દુશ્મની ખતમ કરવી.
examples: The two brothers had not spoken for years.
Their mother urged them to bury the hatchet.
They finally forgave each other.
The family was happy and united again.

idioms.english_meaning: To be caught in the act of doing something wrong.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ખોટું કામ કરતાં રંગે હાથ પકડાઈ જવું.
examples: The boy was taking sweets without asking.
His mother caught him red-handed.
He could not deny it at all.
He apologised and promised to ask next time.

idioms.idiom: Don't count your chickens before they hatch
idioms.english_meaning: Do not assume success before it actually happens.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પરિણામ આવ્યા પહેલાં સફળતા માની ન લેવી; ઈંડા સેવાય તે પહેલાં મરઘી ગણવી નહિ.
examples: He started spending the prize money in his mind.
But he had not even won yet.
Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
In the end, someone else won the prize.

idioms.english_meaning: Something that is easy to suggest but hard to actually do.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કહેવું સહેલું પણ કરવું અઘરું.
examples: Everyone told me to quit my bad habit.
But that is easier said than done.
Breaking an old habit takes real effort.
Slowly, with discipline, I managed it.

idioms.english_meaning: To feel uncomfortable in an unfamiliar situation.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: અજાણ્યા વાતાવરણમાં અસહજ લાગવું; પાણી બહારની માછલી જેવું.
examples: At the formal party, he knew no one.
He felt like a fish out of water.
He did not know how to behave there.
Soon a kind guest helped him settle in.

idioms.english_meaning: To fail suddenly and completely.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સંપૂર્ણપણે અને ભારે રીતે નિષ્ફળ જવું.
examples: The poorly planned event went down in flames.
Nothing happened the way it was supposed to.
The organisers were deeply embarrassed.
They promised to plan better next time.

idioms.english_meaning: To be extremely kind and generous.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ખૂબ દયાળુ અને ઉદાર સ્વભાવ હોવો; સોના જેવું હૃદય.
examples: She always helps anyone in need.
She truly has a heart of gold.
She often donates to the poor quietly.
Everyone in the town loves her.

idioms.english_meaning: To hope strongly that something good will happen.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સારું થાય એવી આશા રાખવી; શુભ થવાની દુઆ કરવી.
examples: My results are coming out tomorrow.
I am keeping my fingers crossed.
I have worked hard all year.
I just hope everything goes well.

idioms.english_meaning: To tell something briefly, leaving out the details.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ટૂંકમાં વાત કહેવી; લાંબી વાતનો સાર કહેવો.
examples: He started narrating the whole incident.
To make a long story short, the car broke down.
We had to wait for two hours for help.
Finally we reached home safely.

idioms.english_meaning: After a bad experience, one becomes very cautious next time.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: એક વાર દઝાયા પછી માણસ બમણો સાવધ થઈ જાય છે; દૂધનો દાઝ્યો છાશ ફૂંકીને પીએ.
examples: He once lost money in a fake scheme.
Now he checks everything twice before investing.
Once bitten, twice shy.
His caution protects him now.

idioms.english_meaning: Regular practice leads to mastery and improvement.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સતત અભ્યાસથી માણસ નિપુણ બને છે; મહાવરો માણસને પૂર્ણ બનાવે છે.
examples: At first she played the piano badly.
But she practised a little every day.
Practice makes perfect, after all.
Now she plays beautifully.

idioms.idiom: Put your foot in your mouth
idioms.english_meaning: To say something embarrassing or tactless by mistake.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ભૂલથી અણઘટતું કે શરમજનક બોલી નાખવું.
examples: He asked about her job without knowing she was fired.
He really put his foot in his mouth.
The room went awkwardly silent.
He quickly apologised for his mistake.

idioms.english_meaning: A person who is loved and cherished above all others.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: આંખનો તારો; સૌથી વ્હાલું વ્યક્તિ.
examples: His little daughter is the apple of his eye.
He spends every free moment with her.
He cannot bear to see her sad.
She means the whole world to him.

idioms.english_meaning: A lot of unnecessary anger or worry about a very small matter.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: નાની વાતનું મોટું તોફાન; વાતનું વતેસર કરવું.
examples: The neighbours argued over a parked bicycle.
It was really a storm in a teacup.
By evening they had both forgotten about it.
Such small fights rarely matter.

idioms.english_meaning: To make a bad situation even worse by doing something more hurtful.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ઘા પર મીઠું ભભરાવવું; દુઃખમાં ઓર વધારો કરવો.
examples: He missed the bus and got drenched in the rain.
To add insult to injury, he had forgotten his wallet.
Nothing seemed to go right that day.
He just laughed at his own bad luck.

idioms.idiom: At the drop of a hat
idioms.english_meaning: Immediately and without any hesitation.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: તરત જ, વગર વિચાર્યે; પળભરમાં.
examples: She loves travelling so much.
She will pack her bags at the drop of a hat.
Just one phone call and she is ready to go.
Her spontaneity makes trips exciting.

idioms.english_meaning: When you are in need, you must accept whatever help you get.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જરૂરિયાતમંદ માણસ પસંદગી ન કરી શકે; જે મળે તે સ્વીકારવું પડે.
examples: The shelter offered him an old but warm coat.
It was not his favourite colour.
But beggars can't be choosers.
He gratefully accepted the warm gift.

idioms.english_meaning: To fail, come to an end, or be defeated.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: નિષ્ફળ જવું કે ખતમ થઈ જવું; ધૂળ ચાટવી.
examples: The old computer finally bit the dust.
It would not switch on at all.
We had to buy a new one quickly.
Everything has its lifespan.

idioms.english_meaning: To boast or talk proudly about your own achievements.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પોતાનાં વખાણ પોતે કરવાં; બડાઈ હાંકવી.
examples: He kept telling everyone how talented he was.
He loved to blow his own trumpet.
People soon got tired of his bragging.
True talent rarely needs advertising.

idioms.english_meaning: A way of wishing someone good luck, especially before a performance.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: શુભેચ્છા; સફળ થાઓ (ખાસ કરીને કોઈ પ્રદર્શન પહેલાં).
examples: She was about to go on stage to sing.
Her friends told her to break a leg.
She smiled and felt more confident.
Her performance received loud applause.

idioms.english_meaning: To hold a lasting grudge or feel resentful about something.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મનમાં કડવાશ કે રોષ રાખવો; દ્વેષ સંઘરી રાખવો.
examples: He never got the praise he felt he deserved.
Since then he has had a chip on his shoulder.
He often speaks bitterly about the past.
Letting go would make him much happier.

idioms.english_meaning: To deliberately ignore someone or be unfriendly towards them.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: જાણીજોઈને કોઈની અવગણના કરવી; ઠંડો વ્યવહાર કરવો.
examples: After their argument, she gave him the cold shoulder.
She would not even look in his direction.
He realised he had hurt her feelings.
He apologised, and slowly things improved.

idioms.english_meaning: Being too inquisitive about others' affairs can lead to trouble.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: વધારે પડતી જિજ્ઞાસા મુશ્કેલી નોતરે છે.
examples: The boy kept opening the locked cupboard.
His mother warned that curiosity killed the cat.
Inside was a surprise gift he ruined early.
He learned to be patient after that.

idioms.english_meaning: To be less strict or critical with someone.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ પ્રત્યે થોડી નરમાશ રાખવી; છૂટ આપવી.
examples: The new employee made a small mistake.
The manager decided to cut him some slack.
He was still learning the job, after all.
A little patience helped him improve.

idioms.english_meaning: To argue the opposite side just to encourage discussion or test an idea.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ચર્ચા જગાવવા માટે જાણીજોઈને સામો પક્ષ રજૂ કરવો.
examples: Everyone agreed the plan was perfect.
I decided to play devil's advocate.
I pointed out the risks no one had considered.
It led to a much stronger final plan.

idioms.english_meaning: Wasted or lost completely.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પાણીમાં જવું; નકામું વેડફાઈ જવું.
examples: He spent months on the project.
When it was cancelled, all his effort went down the drain.
He felt disappointed for a while.
But he used the lessons in his next work.

idioms.english_meaning: To set a limit on what you are willing to accept or do.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મર્યાદા નક્કી કરવી; હદ બાંધવી.
examples: She helped her friends with money many times.
But she had to draw the line somewhere.
She politely refused to lend any more.
Setting limits kept her friendships healthy.

idioms.english_meaning: Things obtained easily are also lost easily, so don't worry too much.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સહેલાઈથી આવેલું સહેલાઈથી જાય છે.
examples: He won some money in a small contest.
He spent it all the very next day.
Easy come, easy go, he shrugged.
He did not regret it at all.

idioms.english_meaning: To share a worry or confession to feel relieved.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મનનો ભાર હળવો કરવો; દિલની વાત કહી દેવી.
examples: She had been hiding her worries for weeks.
Finally she got it off her chest.
She told her sister everything.
She felt much lighter afterwards.

idioms.english_meaning: To relax and accept a situation as it happens, instead of resisting it.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પરિસ્થિતિ પ્રમાણે શાંતિથી ચાલવું; પ્રવાહ સાથે વહેવું.
examples: Our travel plans changed at the last minute.
Instead of worrying, we decided to go with the flow.
We ended up discovering a beautiful new place.
Sometimes flexibility brings happy surprises.

idioms.english_meaning: To be unable to help or act because of rules or circumstances.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મજબૂરીને કારણે કંઈ ન કરી શકવું; હાથ બંધાયેલા હોવા.
examples: I wanted to approve his leave request.
But company rules left my hands tied.
I explained the policy to him honestly.
He understood it was beyond my control.

idioms.idiom: Have a lot on your plate
idioms.english_meaning: To have a great deal of work or many responsibilities to deal with.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: માથે ઘણું કામ હોવું; ઘણી જવાબદારીઓ હોવી.
examples: She is managing two projects and a new baby.
She really has a lot on her plate.
Her family helps her whenever they can.
She handles it all with a smile.

idioms.english_meaning: To reach the lowest possible point in a difficult situation.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: તળિયે પહોંચી જવું; સૌથી ખરાબ સ્થિતિએ આવવું.
examples: After losing his job and savings, he hit rock bottom.
He felt there was no way forward.
But that low point became a fresh start.
Slowly he rebuilt his life step by step.

idioms.english_meaning: To take care of things while someone is away.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈની ગેરહાજરીમાં કામકાજ સંભાળી લેવું.
examples: The manager had to leave for an emergency.
He asked me to hold the fort.
I handled all the customers calmly.
Everything ran smoothly until he returned.

idioms.english_meaning: In a very brief and simple way; summarised.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ટૂંકમાં; સારરૂપે.
examples: The report was long and detailed.
In a nutshell, the company made a good profit.
That was the main point everyone needed.
A short summary saved a lot of time.

idioms.english_meaning: Both people involved in a situation share the responsibility.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ઝઘડામાં બંને પક્ષ જવાબદાર હોય છે; તાળી એક હાથે ન પડે.
examples: He blamed his partner for the failed deal.
But it takes two to tango.
Both of them had made mistakes.
They shared the responsibility equally.

idioms.english_meaning: To be extremely happy and excited.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ખુશીથી ઊછળી પડવું; ખૂબ આનંદિત થવું.
examples: The children jumped for joy at the news.
Their summer holidays had finally begun.
They started planning fun activities at once.
The whole house was full of laughter.

idioms.english_meaning: To do what you promised to do.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: આપેલું વચન પાળવું.
examples: He promised to return the book on time.
He always keeps his word.
He returned it exactly as promised.
People trust him because of this habit.

idioms.english_meaning: An informal and humorous way to say someone has died.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મૃત્યુ પામવું (અનૌપચારિક); ઊકલી જવું.
examples: The old film was about a man's last wish.
He wanted to travel before he kicked the bucket.
So he set off on one final adventure.
The story was both funny and touching.

idioms.english_meaning: To learn how to do a particular job or task.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ કામની આંટીઘૂંટી શીખવી; કામ શીખી લેવું.
examples: On her first week, everything felt confusing.
Her seniors helped her learn the ropes.
Within a month she worked confidently.
Now she trains new joiners herself.

idioms.english_meaning: To help someone with something.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મદદ કરવી; હાથ બટાવવો.
examples: The family was shifting to a new house.
The neighbours came to lend a hand.
Together they finished the work quickly.
Kindness makes hard tasks easier.

idioms.english_meaning: Think carefully about the risks before you act.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પગલું ભરતાં પહેલાં વિચારવું; આગળ-પાછળનો વિચાર કરવો.
examples: He almost signed the deal in a hurry.
His friend reminded him to look before he leaped.
He read the terms carefully first.
He avoided a costly mistake that way.

idioms.english_meaning: To no longer be as skilful at something as you used to be.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પહેલાંની આવડત ગુમાવી દેવી.
examples: The famous chef burnt the dish twice.
People wondered if he had lost his touch.
He practised hard for the next contest.
His winning dish proved them wrong.

idioms.idiom: Make hay while the sun shines
idioms.english_meaning: To make good use of an opportunity while it lasts.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: તક હોય ત્યારે તેનો પૂરો લાભ લેવો; લોઢું ગરમ હોય ત્યારે ઘા મારવો.
examples: Business was booming during the festival.
The shopkeeper made hay while the sun shone.
He stocked extra goods and sold them fast.
His profits doubled that season.

idioms.english_meaning: Money is limited and should not be wasted.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પૈસા ઝાડ પર ઊગતા નથી; પૈસા સહેલાઈથી મળતા નથી.
examples: The boy wanted a new toy every week.
His father reminded him that money doesn't grow on trees.
He explained how hard it is earned.
The boy started spending more wisely.

idioms.english_meaning: To stop a problem at an early stage before it grows.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સમસ્યાને શરૂઆતમાં જ ડામી દેવી; કળીમાં જ ચૂંટી નાખવી.
examples: The teacher noticed a small group quarrel.
She nipped it in the bud at once.
She talked to the students before it spread.
Peace returned to the classroom quickly.

idioms.english_meaning: Alert, quick to understand, and good at one's job.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સજાગ અને હોશિયાર હોવું; ચપળ રહેવું.
examples: The new assistant is really on the ball.
She finishes tasks before they are even asked.
She catches errors that others miss.
The whole team relies on her.

idioms.english_meaning: Completely impossible or not allowed.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: સાવ અશક્ય; વિચારવા જેવુંય નહિ.
examples: The children asked to stay out all night.
Their parents said it was out of the question.
Safety came before everything else.
They agreed to come home by ten instead.

idioms.english_meaning: Careful with small amounts of money but wasteful with large ones.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: નાની બાબતે કંજૂસ અને મોટી બાબતે ઉડાઉ.
examples: He refused to spend on regular car servicing.
Later the engine failed and cost a fortune.
He was penny wise but pound foolish.
Small savings led to a big loss.

idioms.english_meaning: To decide how to act as a situation develops, without a fixed plan.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: પરિસ્થિતિ પ્રમાણે નક્કી કરવું; આગોતરી યોજના વગર ચાલવું.
examples: We had no fixed schedule for the trip.
We decided to play it by ear.
Each day we chose where to go next.
The freedom made the journey fun.

idioms.idiom: Rome wasn't built in a day
idioms.english_meaning: Important and great things take time to achieve.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મોટાં કાર્યો સમય માગે છે; ઉતાવળે આંબા ન પાકે.
examples: She wanted to master painting in a week.
Her teacher said Rome wasn't built in a day.
She practised patiently for months.
Her skill improved beautifully over time.

idioms.english_meaning: To keep some money aside for a time of future need.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ભવિષ્યની મુશ્કેલી માટે બચત કરવી; ખરાબ દિવસ માટે સંઘરવું.
examples: She put aside a little money every month.
She believed in saving for a rainy day.
When an emergency came, she was prepared.
Her habit gave her great peace of mind.

idioms.english_meaning: To wait patiently and not take any action yet.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ધીરજથી રાહ જોવી; શાંતિથી બેસી રહેવું.
examples: The flight was delayed due to bad weather.
The staff asked us to sit tight.
We waited calmly in the lounge.
The plane took off after an hour.

idioms.english_meaning: To relax and not worry or work too hard.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: શાંત રહેવું; આરામ કરવો, ચિંતા ન કરવી.
examples: He had been working without any break.
His doctor advised him to take it easy.
He took a short holiday to rest.
He returned feeling fresh and healthy.

idioms.english_meaning: To spend less money because you have less of it.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: ખર્ચમાં કાપ મૂકવો; કરકસર કરવી.
examples: After the pay cut, the family had to tighten their belts.
They cut down on dining out.
They planned every expense carefully.
Within months their savings improved.

idioms.idiom: Two heads are better than one
idioms.english_meaning: Two people working together can solve a problem better than one alone.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: બે માણસનો વિચાર એક કરતાં સારો; સંપથી કામ સારું થાય.
examples: I was stuck on a difficult puzzle.
My friend joined me to help.
Two heads are better than one.
Together we solved it in minutes.

idioms.english_meaning: To be very careful not to upset or offend someone.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: કોઈને નારાજ ન કરવા ખૂબ સંભાળીને વર્તવું.
examples: After the argument, the mood was tense.
Everyone was walking on eggshells around him.
They chose their words very carefully.
Things eased once he calmed down.

idioms.idiom: When the going gets tough, the tough get going
idioms.english_meaning: Strong people work even harder when a situation becomes difficult.
idioms.gujarati_meaning: મુશ્કેલ સમયમાં મજબૂત માણસો વધુ મહેનતથી આગળ વધે છે.
examples: The team was far behind in the match.
But when the going gets tough, the tough get going.
They played with double the energy.
Their comeback stunned everyone.
